chunks: From him, from Al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq, from one of our companions, who said:

Some of the Alawites, who used to belittle him, were mentioned in the presence of Al-Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him). He said: 'Indeed, he is remaining upon what is forbidden.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, how is that, while she is his mother (of the child)?' He said: 'How did he divorce her?' I said: 'How did he divorce her?' He said: 'He divorced her, and that is his religion (custom/practice), so she became forbidden to him.'

key_terms.مُقِيمٌ عَلَى حَرَامٍ: Remaining upon what is forbidden (valid but distinct from ideal practice)
key_terms.يَتَنَقَّصُهُ: To belittle or speak ill of him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on triple divorce without proper conditions in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam Al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of 'following the practice' (*ittiba' al-madhhab*) for non-Shia men, ruling that their triple talaq is effective even if they lack specific Shia conditions for divorce. This highlights the jurisprudential distinction where the Imam validates the external act of divorce based on the husband's own school of thought, rendering the wife permanently forbidden (*muhrimah*) until she marries another man. The context underscores the practical application of talaq validity across different Islamic legal traditions within Shia fiqh.
